title: The Velveteen Rabbit

subtitle.text: On Christmas morning Rabbit looked around the room.
He was inside a stocking over a fireplace.
Across the room stood a pretty tree.
Everything was so exciting and new here!
A boy ran down the stairs.
"Why don't you look in your stocking first?"
He grabbed the velveteen rabbit from the stocking.
Henry and Rabbit played all morning long.
Rabbit was amazed by more new sights and sounds.
He felt warm as Henry held him tightly.
"This is so much fun!" Rabbit thought.
"I want to play with Henry every day."
After dinner Henry and Rabbit played some more.
Henry scooped up Rabbit in his arms again.
He brought Rabbit upstairs to a playroom.
Henry set Rabbit on a shelf.
Rabbit looked around as Henry left.
Other toys were staring at him!
The playroom was filled with toys.
Rabbit saw a soldier and dinosaurs.
There were action figures and stuffed animals.
A red remote control car spun her wheels.
"Vroom!" she said in a friendly voice.
But a robot glared at Rabbit.
He was tall and shiny with angry metal eyebrows.
Rabbit gulped and tried to smile.
"Um, well, I'm happy to meet all of you.
And I really like playing with Henry!"
"You won't last long around here, Rabbit.
You're not made of strong stuff like me."
He laughed. "You don't even have legs!"
Rabbit's body was just a cloth sack.
He had no legs and no feet.
His coat was shabby and worn.
Horse's kind voice made Rabbit feel better.
"Soft toys like us last the longest," he whispered.
The next day Henry took Rabbit all over the house.
He stomped Rabbit through a dinosaur jungle.
The dinosaurs roared like angry beasts.
He loved sliding down the stairs.
He loved watching birds out the window.
He especially loved playing with Henry.
That night Henry put all the toys away.
And my tail lost some of its fluff."
"I knew you were weak!" Robot said.
We are alive in a child's mind forever."
Horse smiled. "Maybe you will one day."
Robot laughed. "You'll never be real, Rabbit!
You can't do any cool stuff—like I can!"
Rabbit loved watching Car zoom around.
But he wanted to play with Henry too.
"My turn will come soon," Rabbit thought.
She went around a tower made of blocks.
Henry grinned. "This car is so fast!"
Car slammed hard into the tower.
Wooden blocks tumbled down onto Car.
"I'm okay," Henry said. "But my car isn't!"
Car's front bumper had a crack.
"Let's see if we can fix it," Dad said.
Rabbit watched while Dad taped the bumper.
Dad spent a long time working.
At last Henry picked up the control again.
The car made a sound but didn't move.
We tried to fix it, but it's broken."
Rabbit's coat looked a little shabby.
"One day Dad might take me away too!"
It was a few days later.
Soldier stood at his post near the window.
"Oh no!" Several toys gasped and hid.
Rabbit sat on a shelf. "Who's Vicky?"
"She's going to rip you to pieces!"
Then a girl with pigtails came in.
She was holding a red drone.
"She doesn't look so bad," Rabbit thought.
Vicky suddenly stopped in front of Rabbit.
Vicky plopped the drone on the floor.
She tied Rabbit to the top of it with string.
The drone shot up into the air.
Rabbit fell off and went tumbling down.
Rip! His right shoulder tore open.
Henry took Rabbit into the kitchen.
Mom sighed. "I'll see what I can do."
"What if Mom can't fix me?" Rabbit thought.
Mom got some thread and a needle.
"I can't watch!" Henry ran out of the room.
"Henry sure loves you," Mom said softly.
Rabbit felt a warm glow inside.
Later Mom put Rabbit back in the playroom.
"Maybe I'll be real soon!" Rabbit said.
You're just like the rest of us."
Robot made him so angry sometimes!
But he didn't want to fight.
One night Rabbit fell asleep and started to dream.
"This must be fairy dust!" he thought.
Horse often told Rabbit stories about fairies.
He jumped out the playroom window.
Beautiful white flowers danced in the grass.
Rabbit floated up to the clouds.
He hopped as high as he could.
He hopped to one star and another.
Then he hopped all the way to the moon.
Rabbit was smiling when he woke up.
Only one other toy was awake—Robot.
"I had legs and feet," Rabbit said.
"I hopped to the stars and the moon!"
"Robot, can't you try to be nice?
Henry is nice to all of us.
And I'm nice to everyone too."
"We know Henry loves you the most.
Not all of us can be soft and cuddly."
Rabbit blinked as Robot spun away.
"Maybe he wants Henry to hold and hug him too."
At night Rabbit usually slept in the playroom.
But one night Henry left Rabbit in his room.
Henry tossed and turned in bed.
Mom came in and felt Henry's forehead.
She gave Henry medicine and stroked his back.
Mom saw Rabbit and brought him over.
Henry's body felt hot and wet.
He lay still until Henry fell asleep.
Rabbit saw the moon shining through the window.
It looked just like his dream.
Rabbit stared at the fairy dust.
Maybe it will make Henry feel better!"
Rabbit gently rubbed his paw on Henry's arms.
Rabbit stayed up all night long, watching Henry.
"Will the magic dust work?" he thought.
The next morning Mom came back.
So, at first, he wasn't worried.
But then Mom looked closely at Rabbit.
He'll probably fall apart in the washing machine.
We might need to get rid of him."
You can't get rid of Rabbit!"
"I'll try to give him a wash."
Mom tossed Rabbit inside the washing machine.
Water and soap poured over him.
The machine spun round and round.
But then Mom put him in the dryer!
Rabbit tumbled and twisted some more.
His coat was thin and bare.
I'm not made of strong stuff.
It's as big as a small house!"
"I bet the family is going on a trip."
All morning the family rushed around.
Dad came into the playroom, smiling.
"Who's ready for the best road trip ever?"
Then Dad and Henry left the playroom.
Henry ran back into the playroom.
"I almost forgot you, Rabbit!" he said.
Robot gave Rabbit a mean look.

family and Rabbit got into the RV. Mom
they drove and drove and drove. Rabbit
loved watching the trees go by. Suddenly
Rabbit spotted something alongside the road. "Wait
As Mom kept driving, Henry fell asleep.
But Rabbit stayed awake with so many questions.
What were the outside rabbits like?
Did they have a kid to play with too?
Would he meet any real rabbits on this trip?
In the afternoon the RV stopped.
Ahead was a clear blue lake.
He looked around and saw squirrels.
"Maybe I'll see real rabbits too!" he thought.
"Can we go swimming now?" Henry asked.
Then everyone went to the lake.
Henry set Rabbit on the ground.
Henry ran to the water and splashed in.
Rabbit looked around while the family swam.
"They make me want to run fast.
But . . ." He looked down and sighed.
The breeze felt cool and gentle.
When he opened them again, he gasped.
Several creatures were staring at him!
The creatures had pink noses and long ears.
"Look at their strong feet!" Rabbit thought.
"Come play with us," a brown rabbit said.
"Yes! Jump high like me!" a white rabbit said.
The rabbits were all staring at Rabbit.
"Where are your legs and feet?" the white rabbit asked.
Rabbit sighed. "I don't have legs or feet."
"He has a nose like a rabbit," the spotted one said.
Rabbit watched and then tried to jump.
But no matter how hard he tried . . .
If you want to try again, look for us."
"We live near the field," the white one said.
He watched the rabbits hop away.
"Will I ever hop and jump like them?"
One morning Henry put Rabbit on a tree stump.
"It's our last day here," Henry said sadly.
He missed his friends from the playroom.
But then he remembered the outside rabbits.
"I'll never see them again," he thought.
Henry left Rabbit outside while he helped his parents.
The family was cleaning and packing up the RV.
Rabbit waited for Henry to come outside and get him.
But Henry stayed on the RV.
Then Dad started the loud engine.
He watched in horror as the family drove away.
But the RV kept moving away from him.
Soon Rabbit couldn't see it anymore.
Every sound and shadow was spooky to Rabbit.
"I'll never see Henry again," Rabbit thought.
Henry jumped out and ran to Rabbit.
"I'm so sorry, Rabbit," he said, crying.
Dad laughed. "All this fuss for a toy!"
"Rabbit is not a toy," Henry said.
He'll be my real friend forever!"
Rabbit felt a warm glow inside.
"Henry said I was real!" he thought.
"Wait until I tell Horse and the others!"
"Henry said I'm real!" he told everyone.
"Then where are your feet and legs?"
But he couldn't forget what Robot said.
Rabbit had no feet or legs.
So how could he be real?
"I am real," he told himself firmly.
"And someday I will hop and jump."
But all he could do was flip over.
One day Robot was watching Rabbit.
That night he talked to Horse.
Horse smiled. "You don't have to move.
You'll live forever in his mind."
But Rabbit wanted to be real like the outside rabbits.
He wanted to hop and jump and play outside.
"So, I'll just try to be the best friend ever."
Rabbit tried to be a good friend.
Then, in the fall, something changed.
Henry left the house every day with a backpack.
He was gone for hours and hours.
One day Rabbit sat on the chair.
Soldier stood near the open window.
"There are lots of leaves on the ground," Soldier said.
"Soon the family will have to rake them."
"Is Henry coming back yet?" Rabbit asked.
"I'll try to move to the window," he thought.
"Then I can watch for Henry myself!"
He twisted this way and that.
"I'm trying to move to the window," Rabbit said.
"I want to watch for Henry myself."
His ears got caught, and he tried to wiggle free.
Rabbit was still trapped in the bush.
"Henry will come home soon," he thought.
But Henry went right past Rabbit.
Rabbit sighed as Henry ran inside the house.
"Maybe he'll come out again later," he thought.
By now the afternoon air was chilly.
Just then the whole family came into the yard. They
were holding rakes and other things. "I'll
rake up all these leaves!" Henry yelled. "Let's
a loud blowing machine started up. Dad
came closer, blowing away leaves. The
blowing machine sent leaves flying everywhere. "Oh
no!" Rabbit thought as the bush shook hard. Then—
Rabbit flew out of the bush.
He tumbled into a pile of leaves.
More leaves fell on top of him.
Henry was making a pile of leaves.
He laughed as he jumped onto the pile.
For a moment Rabbit forgot his worries.
He was happy to hear Henry laughing.
"Henry will find me soon," Rabbit thought.
Suddenly Dad came over with a big bag.
Then Mom came with a rake.
The rake shot into the pile.
It scooped leaves into the bag.
Mom carried the bag to the curb.
"The garbage truck will pick this up tomorrow," she said.
The sun was setting as everyone went inside.
That night Rabbit saw Henry's shadow in the playroom.
Henry was walking back and forth.
"Is he looking for me?" Rabbit thought.
"I'm here, Henry! It's cold!" he called.
"Tomorrow the garbage truck will carry me away," he thought.
A tear fell from Rabbit's eye.
The wet spot began to glow.
The white flower glowed in the moonlight.
She had short hair and long wings.
Rabbit floated out of the bag.
He landed gently on the grass.
"You're a good friend to Henry," the fairy said.
"Because of that, you will become a real rabbit."
Rabbit gasped and looked down at his sack body.
"Real . . . like the outside rabbits?" he said.
The fairy laughed. "Yes, real like those rabbits.
I will sing you a lullaby."
But Rabbit was much too excited to sleep.
"I'll need legs and feet like the real rabbits.
Now close your eyes and let the magic come."
He felt fairy dust swirl around him.
Rabbit thought of the blue lake and green mountains.
He felt the fairy kiss his nose.
Then he drifted off to sleep.
When Rabbit woke up, he smelled pine trees.
"What are you doing here?" he asked.
"What are you doing here?" the white rabbit said.
Rabbit looked around and saw the mountains.
He saw lots of pine trees.
"I think a fairy brought me here," Rabbit said.
"Well, something magical happened," the spotted one said.
"So you can play with us!" the white rabbit said.
He had real feet and long legs!
Rabbit jumped and hopped with his new feet.
All the rabbits jumped and cheered.
They chased each other across the field.
They played together until the sun went down.
Rabbit followed the others to a warm, cozy den.
Everyone curled up, ready for bed.
Rabbit fell asleep, still thinking of his friend.
Rabbit was happy in his new home.
He was clever at finding the sweetest grass.
He learned how to hide from hawks.
On rainy days the rabbits stayed inside.
That's when Rabbit thought about Henry and the toys.
"I wonder how everyone is doing," Rabbit thought.
One day the rabbits heard a sound.
"It's the big metal monster again!" the spotted rabbit said.
"It's called an RV," Rabbit said wisely.
"It's fun to ride in an RV!"
Rabbit hopped with joy. "It's Henry and his parents!"
Henry saw a rabbit hopping nearby.
"It looks just like my old velveteen rabbit!"
I wonder what happened to Rabbit."
Henry and Rabbit stared at each other for a while.
Henry reached down to pet him.
"Rabbit was a good friend," Henry said softly.
Rabbit watched Henry and his parents walk away.
He thought of all their happy times together.
